message.content:
### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip or reorder steps if you’re comfortable with certain parts (e.g., you already have a pre‑assembled case or you’re using a custom water‑cooling loop). The goal is to give you a clear, logical flow from unboxing to first boot.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Decide what you’ll use the PC for (gaming, video editing, general use) and set a budget. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to estimate costs and check compatibility. |
| **2** | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | You’ll need a Phillips‑head screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended), a clean, flat surface, and plenty of light. | Keep the area dust‑free; a microfiber cloth helps. |
| **3** | **Unbox & Inspect** | Check that all components are present: case, motherboard, CPU, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, cooling system, cables, manuals. | Verify serial numbers and warranty info. |
| **4** | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs for the motherboard, and set up any case fans or radiators. | Label standoffs for front/back orientation. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Secure the PSU in its tray, route cables, and connect the main 24‑pin and 8‑pin EPS cables to the motherboard. | Keep cables tidy; use Velcro ties or zip ties. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align the motherboard with the standoffs and screw it in place. | Double‑check that the I/O shield fits the case’s back panel. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Open the CPU socket latch, align the CPU (gold triangle), place it gently, and lock the latch. | Avoid touching the pins or contacts. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | If your cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount. Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | Ensure the cooler is firmly seated; check fan orientation. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM** | Open the RAM slots, align the notch, and press until the clips click. | Install in the recommended slots (often 1 & 3 for dual‑channel). |
| **10** | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use the drive trays or brackets. | Label SATA cables if you’re using multiple drives. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers, insert the GPU, and secure it with screws. | Connect any required PCIe power cables from the PSU. |
| **12** | **Connect Front Panel & USB Cables** | Attach the case’s front‑panel connectors (power button, reset, USB, audio) to the motherboard headers. | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin layout. |
| **13** | **Cable Management** | Route cables behind the motherboard tray, use cable ties, and keep airflow unobstructed. | Avoid blocking the rear fan or radiator. |
| **14** | **Double‑Check All Connections** | Verify that every cable is firmly connected, no loose screws, and no wires blocking fans. | Turn off the PSU before touching anything. |
| **15** | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | Connect a monitor, keyboard, and mouse. Power on the system. Enter BIOS/UEFI (usually F2, Del, or Esc). | Set boot priority to your OS drive, enable XMP for RAM, and check temperatures. |
| **16** | **Install Operating System** | Boot from a USB installer (Windows, Linux, etc.), format the drive, and follow on‑screen prompts. | Keep drivers handy (motherboard chipset, GPU). |
| **17** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Install chipset, GPU, audio, and network drivers. Run Windows Update or your distro’s update manager. | Reboot after major driver installs. |
| **18** | **Test & Benchmark** | Run a stress test (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench) to ensure stability. Monitor temperatures and voltages. | If temperatures are high, re‑apply thermal paste or improve airflow. |
| **19** | **Final Clean‑Up** | Remove any packaging, tidy cables, and ensure the case is sealed. | Store spare screws and cables in a labeled bag. |
| **20** | **Enjoy Your New PC!** | Install your favorite software, games, or productivity tools. | Keep your system updated and back up important data. |

---

#### Quick Checklist (Printable)

- [ ] Case standoffs installed
- [ ] PSU secured & cables routed
- [ ] Motherboard mounted
- [ ] CPU seated & cooler installed
- [ ] RAM installed
- [ ] Storage installed
- [ ] GPU installed
- [ ] Front panel connectors attached
- [ ] All cables connected
- [ ] BIOS settings verified
- [ ] OS installed
- [ ] Drivers updated
- [ ] System tested

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **CPU not seated** | Double‑check alignment, ensure the latch is fully closed. |
| **GPU not recognized** | Verify PCIe power connectors, ensure the card is fully inserted. |
| **High temperatures** | Reapply thermal paste, improve cable routing, add case fans. |
| **No boot** | Check that the PSU is switched on, all cables are connected, and the monitor is set to the correct input. |
| **BIOS not loading** | Reset CMOS (short the jumper or remove the battery for a few minutes). |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build lists, price tracking, compatibility checks.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always keep them handy; they’re often the most reliable source for connector layouts.

Happy building! If you hit a snag or need component recommendations, just let me know.
